entities.name: African Union Commission
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The African Union Commission (AUC) is the secretariat and administrative organ of the African Union, established in 2002 to succeed the Organization of African Unity (OAU). Headquartered in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, the Commission implements AU decisions, initiates AU policies, and manages the day-to-day operations of Africa's primary pan-continental political institution.

The OAU was founded in 1963 by African nationalist leaders including Kwame Nkrumah, Haile Selassie, and Julius Nyerere in Addis Ababa to coordinate decolonization, promote pan-African unity, and prevent external interference in African affairs. The 2002 transformation into the African Union, modeled partially on the European Union, reflected ambitions for deeper integration including a common currency, open borders, and collective security mechanisms.

The AU Commission implements flagship programs including Agenda 2063 (Africa's long-term development vision), the Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) creating the world's largest free trade zone by member countries, and the Africa CDC health emergency coordination. The Commission's enforcement of governance norms — condemning coups, facilitating elections — has been inconsistent, with member states often prioritizing sovereignty over accountability. The Peace and Security Council, a key AU body the Commission supports, has mediated conflicts in Sudan, Somalia, and the DRC.
